# Golden frames of the sealer wire, one `name hex` line each. All integers
# are little-endian. The Rust test `wire::entry_tests` checks that the Rust
# encoders write these bytes and that the Rust decoders read them. The
# sealer test `WireGoldenTest` checks that the Java codecs build the same
# egress bytes from the ingress bytes.
#
# tx_offer_ingress  ingress kind 0, record type 5 (full entry), lane 3
# tx_egress         egress kind 1, index 5, record type 6 (canonical entry)
# relayed_ref       egress kind 15 for the entry at index 5
# feed_gap          egress kind 16, next index 9, next block 4, request id 7
# feed_replay_done  egress kind 4 on the member feed: up to index 9, block 4,
#                   with the request id 7 as a tail; an egress reader reads
#                   it as kind 4 and ignores the tail
# status_76         egress kind 9 with the record-lag tail, the flag byte
#                   (snapshot_follows, 0) and the byte tail
# status_76_snapshot  status_76 with the flag byte at 1 (a snapshot follows)
# status_68         egress kind 9 with the record-lag tail and the flag byte (0)
# status_67         egress kind 9 with the record-lag tail only (the release
#                   before the flag byte)
# txref_ingress     ingress kind 0, record type 0 (reference)
# txref_egress      egress kind 1, index 5, record type 0
tx_offer_ingress
